problem_motivation.content: No existing data on the creep and tensile properties of Ta20Nb20Hf20Zr20Ti20.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: since the literature review revealed no data whatsoever regarding these properties

problem_motivation.content: There is a lack of published data on tensile and creep properties for as-cast Ta20Nb20Hf20Zr20Ti20 under tension, which this study aims to address.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: However, no data whatsoever have been published in reference to tensile properties and creep properties of as-cast Ta 20 Nb 20 Hf 20 Zr 20 Ti 20 under tension. The current paper seeks to fill this gap

prior_approach.content: Previous literature reports compression mechanical property values for this material.
Senkov et al. previously conducted compression tests on the Ta20Nb20Hf20Zr20Ti20 alloy and analyzed its deformation behavior using SEM.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Senkov et al. [ [2] ] conducted compression tests on Ta 20 Nb 20 Hf 20 Zr 20 Ti 20 at room temperature as well as at 600 °C, 800 °C, 1000 °C and 1200 °C under different strain rates and used Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) to investigate the microstructural changes during the deformation process and the fracture mechanisms.

prior_approach.content: Senkov et al. previously produced the alloy via vacuum arc melting, re-melting, HIP, and vacuum annealing.
prior_approach.evidence_span: As reported by Senkov et al. [ [2] , [3] ], the process of producing the Ta 20 Nb 20 Hf 20 Zr 20 Ti 20 alloy consisted of vacuum arc melting followed by re-melting the material three times

prior_approach.content: Hot Isostatic Pressing (HIP) is a common practice used in other studies for closing internal porosity.
prior_approach.evidence_span: HIP is a common practice, involving high temperatures and isostatic pressure and it is used for closing internal porosity [ [12] ]. HIP was applied in other studies as well as reported [ [2] , [3] , [7] , [8] ].

prior_limitation.content: Prior work detected a hexagonal-like phase but failed to identify six additional HCP peaks in the current study's HIP'ed gravity casting.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: Though these researchers reported on a small peak at 2θ = 24.9° indicating the presence of a hexagonal-like phase, they did not refer to the six additional HCP peaks detected in the current study in the case of HIP gravity casting: 2θ = 31.95°, 2θ = 34.28°, 2θ = 37.34°, 2θ = 47.66°, 2θ = 56.79° and 2θ = 63.23°.

prior_limitation.content: Prior work failed to report six HCP peaks detected in the suction-assisted casting.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: Nor did they refer to the following six peaks in the case of the suction-assisted casting: 2θ = 32°, 2θ = 34.3°, 2θ = 36.4°, 2θ = 47.5°, 2θ = 57° and 2θ = 62.6°.

prior_limitation.content: Prior work claimed only a BCC phase was discernible but acknowledged the stability of the BCC phase was unknown.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: Senkov et al. referred to the microstructure of the Ta 20 Nb 20 Hf 20 Zr 20 Ti 20 after undergoing HIP, claiming that only one BCC solid solution was discernible. However, they emphasized that it was not yet known whether the BCC phase is thermodynamically stable at Room Temperature (RT), or whether it is metastable and thus kinetically restricts formation of the low temperature HCP phase due to slow diffusivity

causal_claim.content: The HIP process caused a significant increase in mechanical properties under compression.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The HIP process also led to a considerable increase in the mechanical properties of both materials under compression

causal_claim.content: The HIP process is responsible for the appearance of the HCP phase.
causal_claim.evidence_span: It seems that the HIP process is responsible for the appearance of the HCP phase mentioned above.

causal_claim.content: The HIP process increased the hardness of both castings.
causal_claim.evidence_span: As for the materials that underwent HIP, it is clear that the HIP process increased the hardness of both castings.

causal_claim.content: Rapid cooling in the as-cast alloy prevents the creation of an HCP phase, resulting in a supercooled BCC phase.
causal_claim.evidence_span: In contrast, an HCP phase is not created in the case of the as-cast alloy due to the rapid cooling, resulting in a supercooled BCC phase.

causal_claim.content: The HIP process caused the appearance of an HCP phase in addition to the preexisting BCC stage.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The HIP process, applied to both castings, was found to be responsible for the appearance of an HCP phase in addition to the preexisting BCC stage.

causal_claim.content: The HIP process increased the hardness of both castings, with a larger increase in suction-assisted castings.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The HIP process also increased the hardness of both castings, and in the case of the suction-assisted castings led to a larger increase.

mechanism_principle.content: The hardness increase after HIP is attributed to the secondary HCP phase and its influence on dislocation mobility, similar to precipitation hardening.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: The hardness increase after HIP can be related to the appearance of the secondary HCP phase and its influence on dislocation mobility, similarly to precipitation hardening.

mechanism_principle.content: The difference in hardness between casting types may be due to the distribution of the ZrHf-rich phase.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: The difference between the suction-assisted cast and the gravity cast may be related to the distribution of the ZrHf-rich phase, which is evenly dispersed in the case of the gravity casting while concentrated mainly at the grain boundaries in the case of the suction-assisted casting.

hypothesis_statement.content: The formation of the HCP phase during cooling after HIP is due to a eutectoid reaction or precipitation of the HCP component.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: It is therefore reasonable to derive that when the HIP process of the HfNbTaTiZr alloy ends and the alloy is left to cool at a very slow rate inside the furnace the HCP phase forms out of the original BCC phase, either by a eutectoid reaction or by precipitation.

evidence_result.content: The material exhibits high brittleness under tension, confirmed by fracture observations showing no plastic deformation.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Fractography yielded brittle fracture without any evidence of plastic deformation prior to fracture

evidence_result.content: Hardness values for gravity and suction-assisted castings before and after HIP were measured.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Microhardness tests revealed the hardness of the material to be 323.5 ± 6.5 HV in the case of gravity casting and 330.2 ± 9.8 HV in the case of suction-assisted casting, both before HIP. For the material that underwent HIP, the hardness was found to be 437.2 ± 11.6 HV and 509.1 ± 13.5 HV for the gravity and suction-assisted castings respectively.

evidence_result.content: Elongation to fracture was below detection limits, indicating no measurable plastic deformation.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The elongation to fracture under tension was below the machine’s detection limit and therefore could not be measured.

evidence_result.content: Creep tests at 982 °C resulted in specimen failure after short durations.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Two creep tests at 982 °C were conducted on gravity-cast specimens, the first under a load of 200 MPa and the second under 120 MPa. Both failed after short periods of time of 15 and 90 min, respectively.

evidence_result.content: Fracture surfaces show brittle failure without plastic deformation in both casting methods.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The figures show that the fracture is inter-crystalline in both cases, without any plastic deformation.

evidence_result.content: Creep test fracture surface is brittle and shows oxidation contamination.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Figure 5 and Figure 6 show that the fracture is brittle. As revealed by EDS analysis, the surface is contaminated with oxidation products, mainly at the near-surface regions of the sample.

constraint.content: Elongation measurements were constrained by the detection limit of the testing machine.
constraint.evidence_span: The elongation to fracture under tension was below the machine’s detection limit and therefore could not be measured.

contradiction.content: Compression strength values measured in this study are higher than those reported in the literature.
contradiction.evidence_span: Compression strength values measured for both gravity casting and suction-assisted casting in the current study are higher than those reported in the literature.
